Despite the 4 months Covid 19 Lockdown period in Vanuatu, the team still managed to provide support to selected women market vendors. The monitoring confirmed that there were improved economic status based on increased income, savings, or financial capital (loans, credit, savings, investments) • women market vendors have demonstrated improved socioeconomic security • women market vendors demonstrate agency in financial decision-making in their business and households. • women market vendors are accessing gender-inclusive financial and social services. • women market vendors have increased business and financial skills, such as starting and maintain savings and recording-keeping. women market vendors have developed digital literacy, using online platforms to strengthen their business, like marketing their produce or strengthening and maintaining their network via social media platforms. • women market vendors have diversified market business due to Covid 19 Pandemic
PARTNERSHIP - IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECT INTERVENTIONS
This year, key partnerships were established with organisations for the direct implementation of Outcome 2 project activities. The various organisations selected have technical expertise in empowering urban and rural women market vendors; developing capacities, strengthening institutions, delivering services and training to market vendors; ensuring there is continuous learning and effective knowledge management. The following partners were selected and partnerships strengthened through project implementation: • Government Partners: Partnerships with government as core partnership for sustainability of the outcome 2 implementation. The primary partnerships are with local-level government in the four target countries. Partnerships has been formalized within the four countries.
• MVA Partners: Strengthened collaboration with the 2 MVAs.The MVAs are entry points to selected the rural women market vendors and farmers to attend the financial literacy trainings, business management trainings and the agriculture value addition trainings and protective cropping trainings. The MVAs also supported the planning, coordination and implementation of Outcome 2 activities.
• Private Sector Partners: UNDP continued to strengthen and maintain close coordination and collaboration with ANZ Pacific, Vodafone Fiji, Digicel Pacific. The partnership includes support from the financial institution and digital enterprises to help create market access, and deliver services for women market vendors.
• UN Agencies: Strengthened partnership between UNWomen, UNDP and UNCDF on financial literacy and financial skills training and Parametric microinsurance ; FAO for agricultural support.
Output 2.1: Market vendors have increased agency over financial decision making in their business (vending and other businesses).
Vanuatu: ? Supported 34 women market vendors in Santo through Money Minded Financial Literacy training with ANZ Bank. The training included basic awareness on the use of ANZ App, including other services provided by the Bank. ? Supported 43 women market vendors in Efate through Financial Literacy training with ANZ Bank
Output 2.2: Increased access of market vendors to gender inclusive financial services including access to savings, credit, payments, micro insurance, digital services, and other services/ livelihood protection actions Vanuatu: In Santo, the 34 women market vendors were able to access the following services: ? Vanuatu National Provident Fund, resulting in 10 signing up for Voluntary saving. The session also included awareness on the various services provided for the Informal Sector, including awareness on savings, educational loans, death benefits product.
? Department of Cooperative services, resulting in the rural women market vendors gaining knowledge on the financial literacy and business management options provided by the Department.
? VanCare Insurance that covers term life cover, funeral and personal accident and fire. The package will ensure the women market vendor and farmers are able to access it at an affordable amount especially during unplanned events.
? Vodafone MVatu App that ensures the rural women market vendors are able to send and receive money locally and internationally and also pay their VNPF Contribution
? Digicel – MyCash App that ensures the rural women market vendors are able to send and receive money locally and internationally. The App is saved on their mobile phones, and after selling each day, the vendor deposits the money to be saved in “MyCash” account, and then withdraws as and when needed.
Output 2.3: Market vendors business is improved and more resilient as a result of an increase in business and financial skills (savings and recording) and access to digital literacy and online platforms
Vanuatu: ? Supported 24 rural women market vendors in Santo on Agricultural pest and disease, soil care and plant nutrients. Value addition training provided options for the rural women market vendors to preserve meat, salted meat, pawpaw pickle, vegetable pickle, tomato chutney, fruit jams.
? Supported 34 rural women market vendors in Santo, access Value Addition Trainings by the Department of Industry. The topics covered included food safety, packing and labelling, proper sterilization of Jars, fruit and vegetable pickles and chutneys, instant ginger tea, fruit cordial, fruits in syrup, jams and preservation of vegetables e.g tomatoes and chillies, with product quality, packaging, storage and transportation, traceability and records. The 34 women market vendors acquired new knowledge and skills in value addition from market produce that are not purchased at the market. ? The value addition training also included topics such as pawpaw pickle, vegetable pickle, coconut – virgin oil, pineapple jam, ana mango jam. Export market awareness encouraged farmers to focus on productive sector as most produce are organically grown in Vanuatu. The knowledge sharing enabled the participants to know the government processes, and assistance to access to tap into the export market. The Value Addition trainings by the Department of Cooperative, and topics covered includes pricing of value addition products, adding of mark ups and product costing calculation ? Supported and advocated for the recognition of rural women market vendors in Santo, through the International Rural Women’s Day celebration in Santo. The Joint Celebration between UNDP and UNWomen, were attended by and government partners based in Santo, and the Luganville Municipal Council. The 300 rural women market vendors were recognized for their contribution to food production, processing, cultivation and distribution to consumers. The celebration enabled the rural women to be acknowledged for their contribution to the rural development.
